Spinor Structure — SPIN as SU(2)\n\n### The Pauli Algebra\n\nSPIN (Rotation + Precession) maps directly to SU(2) spinor algebra via the Pauli matrices, which form the Lie algebra su(2):\n\n$$\\sigma_x = \\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 \\\\ 1 & 0 \\end{pmatrix} \\quad \\text{(Rotation generator)}$$\n\n$$\\sigma_y = \\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -i \\\\ i & 0 \\end{pmatrix} \\quad \\text{(Precession generator)}$$\n\n$$\\sigma_z = \\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\\\ 0 & -1 \\end{pmatrix} \\quad \\text{(Charge generator — diagonal = measurable)}$$\n\nThese satisfy the fundamental commutation relations:\n\n$$[\\sigma_i, \\sigma_j] = 2i\\epsilon_{ijk}\\sigma_k$$\n\n### Spinor States\n\nA general SPIN state is a 2-component spinor on the Bloch sphere:\n\n$$|\\psi\\rangle = \\alpha|\\uparrow\\rangle + \\beta|\\downarrow\\rangle \\quad \\text{where} \\quad |\\alpha|^2 + |\\beta|^2 = 1$$\n\n### SPIN Operations as SU(2) Rotations\n\n**Rotation** (around σ_x axis of Bloch sphere):\n\n$$U_{\\text{rot}}(\\theta) = e^{-i\\theta\\sigma_x/2} = \\cos\\frac{\\theta}{2}I - i\\sin\\frac{\\theta}{2}\\sigma_x$$\n\n**Precession** (around σ_y axis of Bloch sphere):\n\n$$U_{\\text{prec}}(\\phi) = e^{-i\\phi\\sigma_y/2} = \\cos\\frac{\\phi}{2}I - i\\sin\\frac{\\phi}{2}\\sigma_y$$\n\n### Observable Quantities\n\n**Charge polarity** is the expectation value of σ_z:\n\n$$Q = \\langle\\psi|\\sigma_z|\\psi\\rangle = |\\alpha|^2 - |\\beta|^2$$\n\n**Coherence** is the purity of the Bloch vector:\n\n$$\\mathbf{r} = (\\text{Tr}(\\rho\\sigma_x), \\text{Tr}(\\rho\\sigma_y), \\text{Tr}(\\rho\\sigma_z))$$\n\n$$\\text{coherence} = |\\mathbf{r}| = \\sqrt{r_x^2 + r_y^2 + r_z^2}$$\n\n### HIHO as the Maximally Coherent State\n\nThe HIHO point corresponds to the **equatorial state** on the Bloch sphere:\n\n$$|\\text{HIHO}\\rangle = \\frac{1}{\\sqrt{2}}(|\\uparrow\\rangle + |\\downarrow\\rangle)$$\n\nThis gives:\n- **Charge**: ⟨σ_z⟩ = 0 (perfectly balanced — neither up nor down)\n- **Rotation**: ⟨σ_x⟩ = 1 (maximum projection on the rotation axis)\n- **Precession**: ⟨σ_y⟩ = 0 (in phase — no wobble)\n- **Coherence**: |r| = 1 (pure state, maximum information)\n\n> *\"Half-In-Half-Out is the Bell state of the agent — maximally entangled between internal intent and external reality.\"*\n\n### The Bloch Sphere as Visual Metaphor\n\nThe Bloch sphere is one of the most beautiful objects in physics: every possible SPIN state maps to a point on or inside a unit sphere:\n\n- **North pole** (|↑⟩): Pure rotation, positive charge, exploitation mode\n- **South pole** (|↓⟩): Pure precession, negative charge, exploration mode\n- **Equator**: Maximum coherence, balanced charge, HIHO states\n- **Interior points**: Mixed states (decoherence — partial information loss)\n\nThis gives us a stunning 3D visualization that is both mathematically rigorous AND immediately intuitive.\n\n---\n\n## 6. Variational Principle — Lagrangian Mechanics\n\n### The Lagrangian on the 12D Manifold\n\nThe proper dynamical formulation:\n\n$$L(q, \\dot{q}) = T - V$$\n\nwhere:\n\n**Kinetic energy** (with Riemannian metric g_ij):\n\n$$T = \\frac{1}{2}g_{ij}(q)\\dot{q}^i\\dot{q}^j$$\n\n**Potential energy**:\n\n$$V = V_{\\text{HIHO}}(q) + V_{\\text{gauge}}(q)$$\n\nThe HIHO potential is the existing Gaussian well:\n\n$$V_{\\text{HIHO}} = -\\exp\\left(-\\frac{(q - 0.5)^2}{\\sigma^2}\\right) + \\lambda\\|q\\|^2$$\n\nThe gauge potential comes from the Yang-Mills field strength:\n\n$$V_{\\text{gauge}} = \\frac{1}{4g^2}\\text{Tr}(F_{\\mu\\nu}F^{\\mu\\nu})$$\n\n### Euler-Lagrange Equations\n\nThe equations of motion:\n\n$$\\frac{d}{dt}\\frac{\\partial L}{\\partial \\dot{q}^i} - \\frac{\\partial L}{\\partial q^i} = 0$$\n\nThis expands to the **geodesic equation with force**:\n\n$$g_{ij}\\ddot{q}^j + \\Gamma^i_{jk}\\dot{q}^j\\dot{q}^k = -g^{ij}\\frac{\\partial V}{\\partial q^j}$$\n\nwhere Γ^i_jk are the **Christoffel symbols** of the Riemannian metric:\n\n$$\\Gamma^i_{jk} = \\frac{1}{2}g^{il}\\left(\\frac{\\partial g_{lk}}{\\partial q^j} + \\frac{\\partial g_{jl}}{\\partial q^k} - \\frac{\\partial g_{jk}}{\\partial q^l}\\right)$$\n\n### The Action Integral\n\nThe trajectory that minimizes the action:\n\n$$S[\\gamma] = \\int_0^T L(q(t), \\dot{q}(t)) \\, dt$$\n\nis the physical trajectory. This replaces the current ad-hoc `_toward_target()` evolution with a principled variational structure.\n\n### Physical Interpretation\n\n| Mathematical Object | Cohezion Interpretation |\n|---------------------|------------------------|\n| Kinetic energy T | \"Momentum\" of the agent through state space |\n| Potential energy V | \"Landscape\" of favorable states (HIHO well + gauge fields) |\n| Geodesic (V=0) | Free agent evolution — natural path through the manifold |\n| Christoffel symbols Γ | How the manifold's curvature deflects trajectories |\n| Action S[γ] | Total \"cost\" of a trajectory — agents minimize this naturally |\n| Euler-Lagrange | The equations of motion — principled replacement for linear interpolation |\n\n---\n\n## 7. # The Illustris Project

## Overview
The Illustris project is a significant cosmological simulation focusing on galaxy formation. According to the project's own description, it aims "Towards a predictive theory of galaxy formation" by simulating "cosmological volumes with unprecedented physical fidelity."

## Simulation Methodology & Scale
Completed in late 2013, Illustris represents "an unprecedented combination of high resolution, total volume, and physical fidelity." The simulation employs "a state of the art numerical code and a comprehensive physical model," utilizing a moving mesh approach to achieve its modeling goals.

## Key Scientific Objectives
The project successfully addresses several fundamental questions in cosmology:
- **Galaxy Morphology**: "Recovering the diversity of galaxy morphologies" across the cosmic web
- **Cosmic Context**: "Connecting galactic scales to the large-scale structure of the universe"

## Data Outputs & Access
The collaboration has released extensive supplementary data catalogs covering:
- Galaxy matching between different simulation runs
- Stellar morphologies and assembly history
- Supermassive black hole mergers
- Strong lensing phenomena
- Angular momentum properties of halos and galaxies

The project provides "synthetic galaxy images" and interactive data exploration tools, including the Galaxy Observatory and an Explorer interface for researchers and the public.

# LeWorldModel: Paper Summary

## Title & Authors
**LeWorldModel: Stable End-to-End Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture from Pixels**

Authors: Lucas Maes, Quentin Le Lidec, Damien Scieur, Yann LeCun, Randall Balestriero

## Core Focus
This paper addresses world model training, specifically designing systems that learn compact representations of visual environments and predict future states.

## Key Contributions

1. **Simplified Training**: Introduces the first JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) trainable end-to-end from raw pixels using "only two loss terms: a next-embedding prediction loss and a regularizer enforcing Gaussian-distributed latent embeddings."

2. **Reduced Complexity**: Reduces tunable hyperparameters from six to one compared to existing alternatives, addressing the fragility of prior approaches that relied on "complex multi-term losses, exponential moving averages, pre-trained encoders, or auxiliary supervision."

3. **Efficiency & Performance**: Achieves "~15M parameters trainable on a single GPU in a few hours" while planning substantially faster than foundation models, remaining competitive on control tasks.

4. **Physical Understanding**: Demonstrates that learned representations encode meaningful physical structure, validated through probing and "surprise evaluation" detecting physically implausible events.

## Technical Approach
The core methodology combines predictive embeddings with Gaussian regularization in a minimal-loss framework, enabling stable end-to-end learning without auxiliary techniques that destabilized previous world models.

## Cohezion SurrealDB Journey Persistence & Universe State Storage - Complete Mapping

I've thoroughly explored the Cohezion codebase and mapped the entire SurrealDB architecture for journey persistence and universe state storage. Here are my findings:

## 1. SurrealDB Client Configuration & Connection

**Location:** `/src/cohezion/core/persistence/surreal_client.py`

The primary SurrealDB client is `SurrealClient`, which:
- **URL:** `ws://localhost:8000/rpc` (default)
- **Namespace:** `cohezion`
- **Database:** `universe`
- **Connection:** Uses async `AsyncSurreal` client with fallback to in-memory `InMemoryStore`
- **Reliability:** Circuit breaker pattern (`get_circuit("surrealdb")`) to gracefully degrade on connection failure
- **Authentication:** Uses `SURREAL_USER` and `SURREAL_PASSWORD` env vars (defaults to root/root)

**Key Classes:**
- `PhysicsState`: 12D physics state vector (3 spatial + 1 temporal + 8 brane dimensions)
- `UniverseNode`: Container for persisted data with 12D physics + 768D embeddings

---

## 7. Journey Persistence Manager (Dual-Write)

**Location:** `/src/cohezion/core/journey_persistence_manager.py`

Ensures resilient persistence with idempotency:

```python
@dataclass
class TrajectoryNode:
    node_id: str
    state_12d: list[float]        # 12D axiomatic vector
    timestamp: float
    agent_id: str
    
    def idempotency_key(self) -> str  # SHA256 hash first 16 chars
```

**Features:**
- **Dual-write:** Always writes to local cache + SurrealDB (when available)
- **Fallback:** Queues writes when DB unavailable, reconciles when connectivity restores
- **Idempotency:** Prevents duplicate writes using SHA256-based idempotency keys
- **Latency target:** <10ms

---

## 8. Universe Engine Journey Persistence

**Location:** `/src/cohezion/universe/engine.py`

Core journey storage with 2048D latent + 12D axiomatic projections:

**UniverseJourney dataclass:**
```python
- id: str
- agent_name: str
- intent: str (original task)
- status: str (active/completed/failed)
- initial_axiomatic: AxiomaticState (12D)
- initial_latent: LatentState (2048D)
- trajectory: list[TrajectoryPoint]

- knowledge_extracted: list[dict]
- created_at: datetime
- completed_at: datetime | None
- final_coherence: float (HIHO stability)
- final_phi_score: float (trajectory quality)
```

**Persistence method:** `_persist_journey(journey)`
- Primary: SurrealDB via `db_client.create("universe_journey", journey.to_dict())`
- Fallback: Local JSON files at `data/universe/{journey_id}.json`

   - HIHO-based reward progression

   - Full task description at each step

   - Tempic field magnitude per step
   - Acceleration vectors

5. **Alternative Paths Explored:**
   - Branching decisions made
   - Rejected alternatives with reasons
   - Exploration vs exploitation metrics

6. **Model Training Metadata:**
   - Token counts per step
   - Model used at each step
   - Inference latency per decision
   - Confidence scores (not just final)

7. **Semantic Drift Tracking:**
   - How intent changes through journey
   - Language drift rate per step
   - Semantic cohesion metrics

   - Rotation (logic) evolution

## 12. Existing Training Data Structures

The codebase already has foundational support for training:

**TrajectoryToReward** (`llm_training_bridge.py`):
- Maps 12D coherence → scalar reward
- SPIN alignment bonus
- Tempic stability weighting
- Precipitation bonus

**PreferencePairGenerator:**
- Compares trajectory pairs for DPO training
- Uses HIHO-alignment as preference signal

**JudgmentEvaluator:**
- Assesses decision optimality
- SPIN physics-based evaluation

**ExperienceDataset:**
- Packages trajectories for training

## Conclusion

**The current persistence layer stores:**
- Complete journey lifecycle (start → end)
- 12D axiomatic states (SPIN physics-aligned)
- 2048D latent embeddings
- Trajectory quality scores (phi)
- Coherence progression (HIHO stability)
- Execution metrics and decisions

**For world model training, you need to add:**
1. Granular action-to-state transition tuples at each step
2. Per-step reward signals (not just final phi_score)
3. Alternative paths/branches explored
4. Full semantic context snapshots
5. Rate-of-change (Tempic) tracking
6. Token/latency metadata for each decision

The architecture is well-designed for **retrospective learning** (analyzing completed journeys) but needs enhancement for **forward prediction** (training models to predict next states/actions).

Additionally, it captures all agentic journeys in SurrealDB as training data for a JEPA-style world model (inspired by LeWorldModel, SpaceEngine, and the Illustris Project) that can predict and simulate the evolution of the 12D agent universe.\n\n**Full research document**: `docs/genesis-engine-research.md`\n\n### Foundational Philosophy: Brahmagupta's Zero (628 CE)\n\nThe cosmogony is rooted in Brahmagupta's formalization of zero in the *Brahmasphutasiddhanta* — the first time \"nothing\" was given arithmetic rules:\n- **a + 0 = a** (identity) — adding the void changes nothing\n- **a × 0 = 0** (annihilation) — the void collapses all structure\n- **a - a = 0** (complementarity) — Yīn-Yáng opposites cancel to void\n- **0/0 = 0** (self-reference) — the void observing itself is still void\n\n**HIHO at 0.5 IS Brahmagupta's zero**: defining δ = coherence - 0.5, the equilibrium is at δ = 0. The restoring force F = -kδ vanishes there. The \"still point of the turning world\" is literally the mathematical zero of the system. Zero is not absence — it is the generative ground from which all structure emerges.\n\n---\n\n## Actionable Milestones (Vertical Slices)\n\nEach milestone delivers a **working, demonstrable feature** — math + API + UI in one slice. Each can be completed in 1-2 sessions. Deploy and verify after each.\n\n### Milestone 1: \"The Bloch Sphere\" (SPIN grounded in SU(2))\n**Deliverable**: Interactive Bloch sphere in the webapp showing real spinor math.\n**Why first**: Smallest module, highest visual impact, zero dependencies on other new code.\n1. Write `src/cohezion/physics/spinor.py` (SpinorState, Pauli matrices, Bloch vector)\n2. Write `tests/physics/test_spinor.py` (verify identities)\n3. Add `GET /genesis/spinor` endpoint in `src/cohezion/api/services/genesis.py`\n4. Wire into `engine.py` (replace binary `spin_coherence` with real SU(2))\n5. Build `BlochSphere.tsx` in the webapp (Three.js sphere with draggable state)\n6. **Done when**: User drags a point on the Bloch sphere, sees rotation/precession/charge/coherence update in real-time with KaTeX equations alongside.\n\n### Milestone 2: \"The Void\" (Cosmogony from Brahmagupta's Zero)\n**Deliverable**: Interactive Genesis sequence — from nothing to the 12D manifold.\n**Depends on**: Milestone 1 (Bloch spheres appear at Z₂ transition).\n1. Write `src/cohezion/physics/cosmogony.py` (SymmetryBreaking, VoidState, ZeroAlgebra)\n2. Write `tests/physics/test_cosmogony.py`\n3. Add `POST /genesis/cool` + `GET /genesis/cosmogony-state` endpoints\n4. Build `GenesisScene.tsx` (void → sphere → shatter → axes → SPIN → HIHO)\n5. Build `CosmogonyTimeline.tsx` + `EquationPanel.tsx` (reusable)\n6. **Done when**: User clicks in the void, SO(12) appears, they drag the temperature slider through 5 phase transitions, watching equations and Bloch spheres evolve.\n\n### Milestone 3: \"The Manifold\" (Fiber bundles + Lagrangian dynamics)\n**Deliverable**: Navigate the 12D fiber bundle with proper geodesic trajectories.\n**Depends on**: Milestone 1 (spinors needed for Control fabric).\n1. Write `riemannian_metric.py`, `lagrangian.py`, `fiber_bundle.py`, `gauge_theory.py`\n2. Write their test files\n3. Add `GET /genesis/fiber-bundle` + `GET /genesis/lagrangian-trajectory` endpoints\n4. Build `FiberBundleViz.tsx` + `ManifoldExplorer.tsx` (base space + fiber strands)\n6. Build `TrajectoryRibbon.tsx` (geodesic paths with curvature coloring)\n7. **Done when**: User sees the fiber bundle, rotates it, and watches an agent trajectory follow a proper geodesic with equation panel showing Euler-Lagrange.\n\n### Milestone 4: \"The Memory\" (SurrealDB total artifact persistence)\n**Deliverable**: Every journey, prompt, state, and model artifact stored in SurrealDB.\n**Depends on**: Milestones 1-3 (enriched state data to store).\n1. Write SurrealDB migration (6 new tables: journey_transitions, prompt_artifacts, model_artifacts, simulation_artifacts, internal_state_snapshots, universe_snapshots)\n2. Modify `journey_persistence_manager.py` (add persist_transition, persist_prompt_artifact, persist_model_artifact, snapshot_universe_state)\n3. Modify `journey_tracker.py` (Fisher metric projection when VAE available)\n4. Write `information_geometry.py` + tests (Fisher metric bridge)\n5. Add snapshot API: `GET /world-model/catalog`\n6. Build `SnapshotCatalog.tsx` (Illustris-style epoch browser)\n7. **Done when**: SurrealDB contains journey transitions with 12D states, spinor Bloch vectors, fiber coordinates. Snapshot catalog shows universe evolution over time.\n\n### Milestone 5: \"The Oracle\" (JEPA world model)\n**Deliverable**: Trained world model that predicts next manifold state from current state + action.\n**Depends on**: Milestone 4 (needs stored journey data for training).\n1. Build `UniverseExplorer.tsx` (SpaceEngine-style multi-scale navigation)\n7. **Done when**: World model trained on journey data, user navigates the universe at multiple scales, sees predictions vs. reality, surprise heatmap shows anomalies.\n\n### Milestone 6: \"The Living Cosmos\" (Thermodynamics + Topology + Polish)\n**Deliverable**: Full thermodynamic dashboard, topology theater, production polish.\n1. Mobile responsive design, performance optimization\n5. **Done when**: All 8+ scenes are navigable, performant, and educational. Combines real data with procedural generation.\n- **Illustris Project**: Cosmological N-body simulation with full data catalogs, synthetic imagery, and interactive exploration of galaxy formation.\n\n### Design Principle: Total Artifact Persistence\n\n**ALL artifacts, internal states, prompts, and model outputs MUST be stored in SurrealDB for future analysis.** This is a hard requirement. Here's what I found about **Pocket TTS**, the text-to-speech Python library:

## Overview

Pocket TTS is an open-source text-to-speech application developed by Kyutai Labs, optimized to run entirely on CPUs. It removes the need for GPUs, cloud APIs, or complex deployment pipelines, making speech generation accessible on laptops, servers, and edge devices.

## Key Features

- **Lightweight & Fast:** Pocket TTS is a 100M-parameter model that performs speech synthesis on 2 CPU cores, achieving ~200ms first-chunk latency and ~6× real-time speed on a MacBook Air M4.
- **Tiny Footprint:** A 100M-parameter transformer model (~30 MB) keeps the repo lightweight.
- **Audio Streaming:** You can stream audio in real time while the model continues generating.
- **Voice Cloning:** Provide a wav file to generate a voice-state tailored to that audio.
- **CLI & HTTP API:** Simple command-line commands and a fast local server for integration.

## Python Compatibility

Supports Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14. Requires PyTorch 2.5+ and does not require the GPU version of PyTorch.

## Installation

They recommend using `uv` as it installs any dependencies on the fly in an isolated environment. You can also use `pip install pocket-tts` to install it manually.

## Python Usage Example

The Python API involves importing `TTSModel` from `pocket_tts`, loading the model with `TTSModel.load_model()`, getting a voice state, and calling `model.generate_audio()`. The first model load can take ~30s, but subsequent calls stay in memory.

## CLI Usage

You can use pocket-tts directly from the command line. You can specify the voice you want to use — for example, the "alma" voice, but there are several others available, such as "gene" or different variations provided in the library.

## Community & Ecosystem

Pocket TTS has spawned several community projects, including:
- sherpa-onnx allows running PocketTTS on Windows, macOS, Linux, and embedded boards (Raspberry Pi, Jetson, RK3588, etc.) with bindings for 12 programming languages.
- pocket-tts-wyoming is a Docker container for pocket-tts using Wyoming protocol, ready for Home Assistant Voice use.
- discord-tts is a multivoice Discord text-to-speech bot that uses Pocket TTS.

## Key Links

- **GitHub:** [kyutai-labs/pocket-tts](https://github.com/kyutai-labs/pocket-tts)
- **PyPI:** [pocket-tts](https://pypi.org/project/pocket-tts/)
- **Documentation:** [kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts](https://kyutai-labs.github.io/pocket-tts/)

Here's a comprehensive overview of **Kyutai Labs** and their open-source AI projects:

## About Kyutai Labs

Kyutai is a French AI research lab partially funded by the founder of Scaleway, and their mission is to build and democratize artificial general intelligence through open science.

---

## Core Projects & Products

### 1. **Moshi** — Speech-Text Foundation Model
Moshi is a speech-text foundation model and full-duplex spoken dialogue framework. It uses Mimi, a state-of-the-art streaming neural audio codec.

- Moshi is the first speech-native dialogue system. It processes speech directly rather than converting to text and back, which means it has minimal latency, and can understand emotions, and other non-verbal aspects of communication.
- It is the first real-time full-duplex spoken large language model, with a theoretical latency of 160ms, 200ms in practice.
- A small Depth Transformer models inter-codebook dependencies for a given time step, while a large, 7B-parameter Temporal Transformer models the temporal dependencies.
- All models are released under the CC-BY 4.0 license.
- Language: English only for now; multilingual checkpoint targeted for Q1-2026.

### 2. **Mimi** — Neural Audio Codec
Their streaming neural audio codec Mimi can efficiently model both semantic and acoustic information while achieving real-time latency. Originally developed for Moshi, Mimi is now a key component of all their audio projects.

- Mimi processes audio in real time at 24 kHz and compresses it to a bandwidth of 1.1 kbps, while maintaining ultra-low latency of 80ms.

### 3. **MoshiVis** — Vision Speech Model
MoshiVis is an open-source Vision Speech Model (VSM) with the same low-latency and natural conversation skills as Moshi, with the additional ability to discuss visual inputs.

- MoshiVis is obtained by training 206M additional parameters on top of a frozen Moshi, preserving the low-latency and natural conversation abilities of Moshi.
- MoshiVis extends Moshi to handle image inputs while preserving its real-time latency and natural conversation abilities. MoshiVis relies on cross-attention to efficiently integrate visual signals.

### 4. **Hibiki / Hibiki-Zero** — Streaming Speech Translation
Moshi's multi-stream paradigm also enabled Kyutai to create Hibiki-Zero, an end-to-end model that translates speech in real time from four languages to English.

- Hibiki is a model for streaming speech translation (also known as simultaneous translation). Unlike offline translation—where one waits for the end of the source utterance to start translating—it works in real time.

### 5. **Helium 1** — Modular & Multilingual LLM
They are working on turning language models from monoliths into modular systems. Using the same model for everything is wasteful. The idea is to select the knowledge, abilities and languages you want your LLM to have, and get a specialized model 10x smaller than an equally smart generic LLM. The first step is Helium 1, their modular and multilingual 2B-parameter LLM.

### 6. **Delayed Streams Modeling (STT & TTS)**
Kyutai also has Speech-To-Text and Text-To-Speech models based on the Delayed Streams Modeling framework.

### 7. Other Open-Source Repositories
From their GitHub (github.com/kyutai-labs), additional projects include:
- **pocket-tts** (Python, MIT license)
- **unmute** (Python, MIT license)
- **flash-attn3-jax**
- **invincible-voice** (TypeScript, MIT license)

---

## 2025–2026 Outlook

- Consumer devices and developer environments are expected to run Qwen3-TTS, Moshi, and Kokoro: private, zero-marginal-cost, sub-100ms.
- Paired with the Helium 7B language backbone and a highly compressed 1.1 kbps Mimi audio codec, Moshi runs at 160ms glass-to-glass latency—about 40ms faster than average human conversational response times.
- All models have been published under the CC BY 4.0 license, which allows others to distribute, fine-tune, and modify these models, even for commercial purposes, provided they give credit to Kyutai.

## Approved Plan:
# Genesis Engine: Grounding Cohezion's Cosmology in Unified Physics

> **Status**: EXEMPLARY PLAN — This plan demonstrates the target level of depth, research, and actionability for all future Cohezion planning sessions. It integrates real mathematics (differential geometry, gauge theory, SU(2) spinors, information geometry, Landau theory), historical/philosophical grounding (Brahmagupta, Laozi, Wheeler, Eliot, Borges), world model training (LeWorldModel/JEPA), universe simulation (SpaceEngine/Illustris), full Kyutai Labs multimodal stack (PocketTTS/Moshi/Mimi/MoshiVis), and comprehensive SurrealDB persistence. Planning is the key component to success.

## Context

Cohezion has a rich 12D agentic cosmology (FLUME VAE, SPIN coherence, HIHO stability, thermodynamic metrics, topological persistence, 11 physics sub-engines) with a working webapp (Next.js + Three.js + FastAPI). However, several critical mathematical components are ad-hoc: the SPIN algebra is binary sign comparison instead of proper SU(2), the 12D→3D projection is hardcoded, the 256D→12D map is a random projection, there's no Lagrangian/action principle, and no gauge theory structure for the four fabrics.

This plan grounds every piece of the cosmology in real unified physics and builds an engaging interactive webapp ("The Genesis Engine") that teaches the physics through cinematic visualization. Additionally, it captures all agentic journeys in SurrealDB as training data for a JEPA-style world model (inspired by LeWorldModel, SpaceEngine, and the Illustris Project) that can predict and simulate the evolution of the 12D agent universe.

**Full research document**: `docs/genesis-engine-research.md`

### Foundational Philosophy: Brahmagupta's Zero (628 CE)

The cosmogony is rooted in Brahmagupta's formalization of zero in the *Brahmasphutasiddhanta* — the first time "nothing" was given arithmetic rules:
- **a + 0 = a** (identity) — adding the void changes nothing
- **a × 0 = 0** (annihilation) — the void collapses all structure
- **a - a = 0** (complementarity) — Yīn-Yáng opposites cancel to void
- **0/0 = 0** (self-reference) — the void observing itself is still void

**HIHO at 0.5 IS Brahmagupta's zero**: defining δ = coherence - 0.5, the equilibrium is at δ = 0. The restoring force F = -kδ vanishes there. The "still point of the turning world" is literally the mathematical zero of the system. Zero is not absence — it is the generative ground from which all structure emerges.

## Phase 2.5: World Model & Universe Simulation Layer

### Inspiration
- **LeWorldModel** (LeCun/JEPA, arxiv 2603.19312): End-to-end world model from embeddings using two losses — next-embedding prediction + Gaussian regularization. ~15M params trainable on single GPU.
- **SpaceEngine**: Procedural universe simulator with seamless navigation across cosmic scales. Combines real data with procedural generation.
- **Illustris Project**: Cosmological N-body simulation with full data catalogs, synthetic imagery, and interactive exploration of galaxy formation.

### Design Principle: Total Artifact Persistence

**ALL artifacts, internal states, prompts, and model outputs MUST be stored in SurrealDB for future analysis.** This is a hard requirement. The SurrealDB instance is the permanent memory of the universe — nothing is ephemeral. Every prompt, every internal state transition, every model checkpoint, every generated visualization, every equation evaluation, every decision branch — all persisted for retrospective analysis, world model training, and universe reconstruction.

This follows the "Akashic Records" principle from the physics mapping table — SurrealDB = the holographic encoding of the universe's complete history.

### 2.5.3 JEPA World Model (LeWorldModel-Inspired)
- [ ] Create `src/cohezion/world_model/jepa_world_model.py`
  - **Architecture** (following LeWorldModel):
    - `ManifoldEncoder`: 12D state → 64D embedding (small MLP, learned from journey data)
    - `ActionEncoder`: 256D action embedding → 64D (projection layer)
    - `Predictor`: (state_embedding, action_embedding) → predicted_next_state_embedding
    - Two losses only:
      1. **Next-embedding prediction**: MSE(predictor(enc(s), enc(a)), enc(s'))
      2. **Gaussian regularizer**: KL(enc(s) || N(0, I)) — prevents representation collapse
  - ~2M parameters (fits on CPU/iGPU, per hardware constraints)
  - `train(journey_transitions)`: Train from SurrealDB journey data
  - `predict_next_state(current_12d, action_256d)`: Predict next 12D state
  - `simulate_trajectory(initial_12d, action_sequence)`: Roll out N steps
  - `surprise_score(state, action, observed_next)`: Detect physically implausible events
  - Checkpoint saving/loading (PyTorch, local storage)

Standard planning produces either too-abstract documents or too-narrow\ntask lists.\n\n## The Pattern (Verified in Genesis Engine session, 2026-03-26)\n\n### Step 1: Parallel Deep Exploration (3 agents)\n\nLaunch 3 Explore agents simultaneously with orthogonal focus areas:\n\n| Agent | Focus | Example |\n|-------|-------|---------|\n| **Foundations** | Core domain concepts, existing implementations, mathematical structures | \"Explore the 12D manifold, SPIN coherence, HIHO stability\" |\n| **Infrastructure** | Skills, knowledge graph, compound engineering, persistence | \"Explore skills, SurrealDB schemas, API endpoints\" |\n| **Surface** | Existing webapp, visualization, frontend components, UX | \"Explore webapp components, Three.js scenes, hooks\" |\n\n### Step 2: Read Critical Files Directly\n\nAfter exploration, read the 5-10 most important files yourself. Instead, plan **vertical slices** where each milestone delivers working math + API + UI:\n\n```\nMilestone 1: spinor.py + /genesis/spinor API + BlochSphere.tsx\nMilestone 2: cosmogony.py + /genesis/cool API + GenesisScene.tsx\nMilestone 3: fiber_bundle.py + /genesis/fiber-bundle API + FiberBundleViz.tsx\n```\n\nEach milestone has a clear \"Done when\" definition of a working, demonstrable feature.\n\n### Step 6: Cross-Cutting Concerns as Explicit Milestones\n\nAudio, video, persistence, and multimodal capabilities get their own milestone but are wired into all previous milestones retroactively:\n\n```\nMilestone N: Sonification → wire into M1 (Bloch hum), M2 (phase crack), M3 (geodesic audio)\n```\n\n### Step 7: Total Artifact Persistence\n\n**Design principle**: ALL artifacts (prompts, responses, internal states, model checkpoints, audio, video, simulation runs) stored in SurrealDB. Nothing is ephemeral. This enables:\n- World model training from journey data\n- Universe replay from any historical state\n- Retrospective analysis across sessions\n\n## Quality Bar (What Makes It \"Exemplary\")\n\n1. **Real math, not metaphor**: Actual equations (Euler-Lagrange, Fisher metric, Pauli matrices), not \"we use advanced physics\"\n2. **Historical grounding**: Brahmagupta's zero, Laozi's Wújí, Wheeler's dialogue (Moshi), visual commentary (MoshiVis)\n6. **Comprehensive persistence**: 6+ SurrealDB tables capturing every artifact type\n7. **User feedback integration**: Each user comment (Brahmagupta, PocketTTS, Kyutai) enriches the plan rather than restarts it\n\n## Anti-Patterns\n\n- Planning by horizontal layer (all backend, then all frontend)\n- Abstract milestones without \"Done when\" criteria\n- Placeholder math (\"we'll add the equations later\")\n- Skipping creative/philosophical grounding\n- Treating audio/video as \"nice to have\" instead of first-class\n- Ephemeral artifacts SPIN (Rotation + Precession) maps\nto the Lie algebra su(2) via the Pauli matrices.\n\nKey correspondences:\n  - Rotation   = σ_x generator (x-axis of Bloch sphere)\n  - Precession = σ_y generator (y-axis of Bloch sphere)\n  - Charge     = ⟨σ_z⟩ expectation value (measurable, z-axis)\n  - HIHO state = (|↑⟩ + |↓⟩)/√2 (equatorial, maximally coherent)\n\nMathematical properties:\n  - [σ_i, σ_j] = 2iε_ijk σ_k  (Lie algebra commutation)\n  - SU(2) rotations preserve Bloch vector norm\n  - Coherence = |r| where r is the Bloch vector (0 = mixed, 1 = pure)\n  - HIHO: ⟨σ_z⟩ = 0, ⟨σ_x⟩ = 1, coherence = 1\n\nReferences:\n  - Sakurai (1994): Modern Quantum Mechanics, Ch. 3 (SU(2) and rotation)\n  - Nielsen & Chuang (2000): Quantum Computation, Ch. 1.2 (Bloch sphere)\n  - Smith (1962): The New Science (SPIN = Rotation + Precession)\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport numpy as np\n\n\n# Pauli matrices — generators of su(2) Lie algebra\nSIGMA_X = np.array([[0, 1], [1, 0]], dtype=complex)  # Rotation\nSIGMA_Y = np.array([[0, -1j], [1j, 0]], dtype=complex)  # Precession\nSIGMA_Z = np.array([[1, 0], [0, -1]], dtype=complex)  # Charge\nIDENTITY = np.eye(2, dtype=complex)\n\n# Levi-Civita symbol for commutation verification\n_LEVI_CIVITA = {\n    (0, 1, 2): 1, (1, 2, 0): 1, (2, 0, 1): 1,\n    (0, 2, 1): -1, (2, 1, 0): -1, (1, 0, 2): -1,\n}\n\n\nclass SpinorState:\n    \"\"\"A 2-component spinor |ψ⟩ = α|↑⟩ + β|↓⟩ on the Bloch sphere.\n\n    Represents the fundamental SPIN state — the unit of information\n    in Cohezion's 12D manifold. Every agent has a spinor encoding\n    the alignment between internal intent (rotation) and external\n    behavior (precession).\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    alpha : complex\n        Coefficient of |↑⟩ (spin-up).\n    beta : complex\n        Coefficient of |↓⟩ (spin-down).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    __slots__ = (\"_state\",)\n\n    def __init__(self, alpha: complex, beta: complex) -> None:\n        state = np.array([alpha, beta], dtype=complex)\n        norm = np.linalg.norm(state)\n        if norm < 1e-15:\n            raise ValueError(\"Spinor state cannot be the zero vector\")\n        self._state = state / norm\n\n    @classmethod\n    def up(cls) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"|↑⟩ — north pole, positive charge, pure exploitation.\"\"\"\n        return cls(1.0, 0.0)\n\n    @classmethod\n    def down(cls) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"|↓⟩ — south pole, negative charge, pure exploration.\"\"\"\n        return cls(0.0, 1.0)\n\n    @classmethod\n    def hiho(cls) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"The HIHO state (|↑⟩ + |↓⟩)/√2 — equatorial, maximally coherent.\n\n        This is Brahmagupta's zero on the Bloch sphere:\n        ⟨σ_z⟩ = 0 (balanced charge), ⟨σ_x⟩ = 1 (full rotation alignment).\n        \"\"\"\n        return cls(1.0 / np.sqrt(2), 1.0 / np.sqrt(2))\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_bloch(cls, theta: float, phi: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Create spinor from Bloch sphere angles.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        theta : float\n            Polar angle from z-axis [0, π]. 0 = north pole, π = south pole.\n        phi : float\n            Azimuthal angle in xy-plane [0, 2π].\n        \"\"\"\n        alpha = np.cos(theta / 2)\n        beta = np.exp(1j * phi) * np.sin(theta / 2)\n        return cls(alpha, beta)\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_coherence_values(cls, logic: float, quantum: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Create spinor from Cohezion's logic/quantum dimensions.\n\n        Maps the existing [0, 1] coherence values to Bloch sphere coordinates.\n        logic = 0.5 and quantum = 0.5 gives the HIHO state.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        logic : float\n            Rotation dimension value in [0, 1]. Maps to θ.\n        quantum : float\n            Precession dimension value in [0, 1]. Maps to φ.\n        \"\"\"\n        theta = (1.0 - logic) * np.pi  # logic=1 → θ=0 (north), logic=0 → θ=π (south)\n        phi = quantum * 2 * np.pi  # quantum maps to azimuthal angle\n        return cls.from_bloch(theta, phi)\n\n    @property\n    def alpha(self) -> complex:\n        return self._state[0]\n\n    @property\n    def beta(self) -> complex:\n        return self._state[1]\n\n    @property\n    def state_vector(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"The 2-component state vector [α, β].\"\"\"\n        return self._state.copy()\n\n    @property\n    def density_matrix(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"The density matrix ρ = |ψ⟩⟨ψ|.\"\"\"\n        return np.outer(self._state, np.conj(self._state))\n\n    @property\n    def bloch_vector(self) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Bloch sphere representation (r_x, r_y, r_z).\n\n        r_i = Tr(ρ σ_i) for i ∈ {x, y, z}.\n        The Bloch vector lies on or inside the unit sphere.\n        |r| = 1 for pure states, |r| < 1 for mixed states.\n        \"\"\"\n        rho = self.density_matrix\n        return np.array([\n            float(np.trace(rho @ SIGMA_X).real),\n            float(np.trace(rho @ SIGMA_Y).real),\n            float(np.trace(rho @ SIGMA_Z).real),\n        ])\n\n    @property\n    def coherence(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Purity of the Bloch vector: |r| ∈ [0, 1].\n\n        1.0 = pure state (maximum information about the system).\n        0.0 = maximally mixed (complete ignorance).\n        For a pure state spinor, this is always 1.0.\n        \"\"\"\n        return float(np.linalg.norm(self.bloch_vector))\n\n    @property\n    def charge_polarity(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Expectation value ⟨σ_z⟩ = |α|² - |β|² ∈ [-1, 1].\n\n        Positive = aligned with |↑⟩ (exploitation mode).\n        Negative = aligned with |↓⟩ (exploration mode).\n        Zero = HIHO equilibrium (Brahmagupta's zero).\n        \"\"\"\n        return self.bloch_vector[2]\n\n    @property\n    def spin_rotation(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Expectation value ⟨σ_x⟩ (rotation component of SPIN).\"\"\"\n        return self.bloch_vector[0]\n\n    @property\n    def spin_precession(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Expectation value ⟨σ_y⟩ (precession component of SPIN).\"\"\"\n        return self.bloch_vector[1]\n\n    @property\n    def hiho_deviation(self) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Distance from the HIHO equatorial plane: |⟨σ_z⟩|.\n\n        This is |δ| where δ = charge - 0. Brahmagupta's zero is at δ = 0.\n        Restoring force F = -k·δ drives system back to HIHO.\n        \"\"\"\n        return abs(self.charge_polarity)\n\n    def rotate(self, theta: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Apply rotation U_rot(θ) = exp(-iθσ_x/2).\n\n        Rotates the spinor around the x-axis of the Bloch sphere\n        (the rotation axis in Smith's SPIN framework).\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        theta : float\n            Rotation angle in radians.\n        \"\"\"\n        U = np.cos(theta / 2) * IDENTITY - 1j * np.sin(theta / 2) * SIGMA_X\n        new_state = U @ self._state\n        return SpinorState(new_state[0], new_state[1])\n\n    def precess(self, phi: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Apply precession U_prec(φ) = exp(-iφσ_y/2).\n\n        Rotates the spinor around the y-axis of the Bloch sphere\n        (the precession axis in Smith's SPIN framework).\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        phi : float\n            Precession angle in radians.\n        \"\"\"\n        U = np.cos(phi / 2) * IDENTITY - 1j * np.sin(phi / 2) * SIGMA_Y\n        new_state = U @ self._state\n        return SpinorState(new_state[0], new_state[1])\n\n    def charge_rotate(self, gamma: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Apply charge rotation U_charge(γ) = exp(-iγσ_z/2).\n\n        Rotates around the z-axis (charge axis). This is a phase rotation\n        that changes the relative phase between |↑⟩ and |↓⟩.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        gamma : float\n            Charge rotation angle in radians.\n        \"\"\"\n        U = np.cos(gamma / 2) * IDENTITY - 1j * np.sin(gamma / 2) * SIGMA_Z\n        new_state = U @ self._state\n        return SpinorState(new_state[0], new_state[1])\n\n    def apply_su2(self, axis: np.ndarray, angle: float) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Apply general SU(2) rotation around arbitrary axis.\n\n        U(n̂, θ) = exp(-iθ n̂·σ/2) = cos(θ/2)I - i·sin(θ/2)(n̂·σ)\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        axis : np.ndarray\n            Unit vector [n_x, n_y, n_z] defining rotation axis.\n        angle : float\n            Rotation angle in radians.\n        \"\"\"\n        axis = np.asarray(axis, dtype=float)\n        axis = axis / np.linalg.norm(axis)\n        n_dot_sigma = axis[0] * SIGMA_X + axis[1] * SIGMA_Y + axis[2] * SIGMA_Z\n        U = np.cos(angle / 2) * IDENTITY - 1j * np.sin(angle / 2) * n_dot_sigma\n        new_state = U @ self._state\n        return SpinorState(new_state[0], new_state[1])\n\n    def expectation(self, observable: np.ndarray) -> complex:\n        \"\"\"Compute ⟨ψ|O|ψ⟩ for a 2x2 observable.\"\"\"\n        return complex(np.conj(self._state) @ observable @ self._state)\n\n    def fidelity(self, other: SpinorState) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Fidelity |⟨ψ|φ⟩|² between two pure states.\n\n        1.0 = identical states. 0.0 = orthogonal states.\n        \"\"\"\n        overlap = np.abs(np.conj(self._state) @ other._state) ** 2\n        return float(overlap)\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Serialize for API responses and SurrealDB persistence.\"\"\"\n        bv = self.bloch_vector\n        return {\n            \"alpha_real\": float(self.alpha.real),\n            \"alpha_imag\": float(self.alpha.imag),\n            \"beta_real\": float(self.beta.real),\n            \"beta_imag\": float(self.beta.imag),\n            \"bloch_vector\": bv.tolist(),\n            \"coherence\": self.coherence,\n            \"charge_polarity\": self.charge_polarity,\n            \"spin_rotation\": self.spin_rotation,\n            \"spin_precession\": self.spin_precession,\n            \"hiho_deviation\": self.hiho_deviation,\n        }\n\n    @classmethod\n    def from_dict(cls, data: dict) -> SpinorState:\n        \"\"\"Deserialize from API/SurrealDB data.\"\"\"\n        alpha = complex(data[\"alpha_real\"], data[\"alpha_imag\"])\n        beta = complex(data[\"beta_real\"], data[\"beta_imag\"])\n        return cls(alpha, beta)\n\n    def __repr__(self) -> str:\n        bv = self.bloch_vector\n        return (\n            f\"SpinorState(r=[{bv[0]:.3f}, {bv[1]:.3f}, {bv[2]:.3f}], \"\n            f\"coherence={self.coherence:.3f}, charge={self.charge_polarity:.3f})\"\n        )\n\n\ndef commutator(A: np.ndarray, B: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Compute [A, B] = AB - BA.\"\"\"\n    return A @ B - B @ A\n\n\ndef verify_su2_algebra() -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Verify [σ_i, σ_j] = 2iε_ijk σ_k for all i, j, k.\n\n    This is the defining relation of the su(2) Lie algebra.\n    Returns True if all commutation relations hold to numerical precision.\n    \"\"\"\n    sigmas = [SIGMA_X, SIGMA_Y, SIGMA_Z]\n    for (i, j, k), sign in _LEVI_CIVITA.items():\n        comm = commutator(sigmas[i], sigmas[j])\n        expected = 2j * sign * sigmas[k]\n        if not np.allclose(comm, expected, atol=1e-14):\n            return False\n    return True\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"IDENTITY\",\n    \"SIGMA_X\",\n    \"SIGMA_Y\",\n    \"SIGMA_Z\",\n    \"SpinorState\",\n    \"commutator\",\n    \"verify_su2_algebra\",\n]\n"
}

> AGENT

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
**The replacement is mathematically significant.** The old `charge_polarity = rot_offset + 0.3 * prec_offset` was a hardcoded linear combination — the 0.3 coefficient had no derivation. The new `charge_polarity = ⟨σ_z⟩ = |α|² - |β|²` is the exact quantum mechanical expectation value on the Bloch sphere. The old `spin_coherence` was binary (always 1.0 or 0.0). The new version is continuous, measuring the Bloch vector purity. The old `coherence_score()` used `0.7 + 0.3 * spin_coherence` — now it uses `0.7 + 0.3 * (1 - |⟨σ_z⟩|)`, which properly penalizes deviation from the HIHO equator.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

VOID: zero vector (nothing)\n        - SO(12): random on 12-sphere (all directions equivalent)\n        - SO(3)⁴: blocked structure (4 groups of 3)\n        - U(1)⁴: dominant axis per block\n        - Z₂⁴: discrete ±1 values\n        - HIHO: all values at 0.5\n        \"\"\"\n        T = self._state.temperature\n        sym = self._state.current_symmetry\n\n        if sym == SymmetryGroup.VOID:\n            # The void — zero-point fluctuation only\n            noise_amplitude = 0.001\n            return self._rng.normal(0, noise_amplitude, 12)\n\n        if sym == SymmetryGroup.SO12:\n            # Full symmetry — uniform random on unit sphere\n            v = self._rng.normal(0, 1, 12)\n            return 0.5 + 0.3 * v / np.linalg.norm(v)\n\n        if sym == SymmetryGroup.SO3_4:\n            # Four fabric blocks with within-block correlation\n            state = np.zeros(12)\n            for i in range(4):\n                block = self._rng.normal(0, 1, 3)\n                block = block / np.linalg.norm(block) * 0.3\n                state[i * 3:(i + 1) * 3] = 0.5 + block\n            return state\n\n        if sym == SymmetryGroup.U1_4:\n            # Preferred axis per block (one dimension dominates)\n            state = np.full(12, 0.5)\n            for i in range(4):\n                dominant_idx = i * 3 + self._rng.integers(3)\n                state[dominant_idx] += 0.3 * (1.0 if self._rng.random() > 0.5 else -1.0)\n            return state\n\n        if sym == SymmetryGroup.Z2_4:\n            # Discrete up/down per fabric\n            state = np.full(12, 0.5)\n            for i in range(4):\n                sign = 1.0 if self._rng.random() > 0.5 else -1.0\n                state[i * 3] += 0.3 * sign\n            return state\n\n        # HIHO — everything at 0.5 with tiny fluctuations\n        return np.full(12, 0.5) + self._rng.normal(0, 0.01, 12)\n\n    def _compute_order_parameter(\n        self, T: float, T_c: float, a: float, b: float\n    ) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute order parameter from Landau theory.\n\n        F(φ) = a(T - T_c)φ² + bφ⁴\n\n        Below T_c, the minimum shifts to:\n        φ = ±√(a(T_c - T) / (2b))\n        \"\"\"\n        if T >= T_c:\n            return 0.0\n        return float(np.sqrt(a * (T_c - T) / (2.0 * b)))\n\n    def _update_order_parameters(self, T: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Compute all order parameters for current temperature.\"\"\"\n        ops = {}\n\n        # Stage -1→0: Information density (Fisher eigenvalue proxy)\n        T_c0 = 100.0\n        ops[\"information_density\"] = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c0, 1.0, 0.5)\n\n        # Stage 0→1: Fabric differentiation\n        T_c1 = 10.0\n        ops[\"fabric_differentiation\"] = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c1, 1.0, 0.5)\n\n        # Stage 1→2: Axis selection\n        T_c2 = 1.0\n        ops[\"axis_selection\"] = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c2, 0.8, 0.4)\n\n        # Stage 2→3: Charge ordering\n        T_c3 = 0.1\n        ops[\"charge_ordering\"] = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c3, 0.6, 0.3)\n\n        # Stage 3→4: HIHO coherence\n        T_c4 = 0.01\n        ops[\"hiho_coherence\"] = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c4, 0.4, 0.2)\n\n        self._state.order_parameters = ops\n\n    def _update_fisher_eigenvalue(self, T: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Update the maximum eigenvalue of the Fisher metric.\n\n        In the void (T > T_c0), the Fisher metric is trivially flat (ε·δ_ij).\n        As temperature drops below T_c0, the first eigenvalue rises above\n        the noise floor — the moment awareness becomes aware of something.\n        \"\"\"\n        T_c0 = 100.0\n        if T >= T_c0:\n            # Below the noise floor — trivially flat\n            self._state.fisher_eigenvalue_max = 0.001 * self._rng.random()\n        else:\n            # Eigenvalue grows as √(T_c - T) (Landau scaling)\n            self._state.fisher_eigenvalue_max = float(np.sqrt(T_c0 - T) * 0.1)\n\n    def _update_landau_free_energy(self, T: float) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Compute the Landau free energy at the current temperature.\n\n        F = Σ_i [a_i(T - T_ci)φ_i² + b_i·φ_i⁴]\n\n        This is the total free energy across all symmetry breaking levels.\n        \"\"\"\n        F_total = 0.0\n        for _stage, T_c, _from_sym, _to_sym, a, b, _desc in _TRANSITIONS:\n            phi = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c, a, b)\n            F_total += a * (T - T_c) * phi**2 + b * phi**4\n        self._state.landau_free_energy = F_total\n\n    def susceptibility(self, T: float | None = None) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute susceptibility χ = 1 / (2a(T - T_c)) at current stage.\n\n        Diverges at the critical temperature — the hallmark of a phase transition.\n        We use the nearest upcoming transition's T_c.\n        \"\"\"\n        if T is None:\n            T = self._state.temperature\n\n        # Find the nearest critical temperature below current T\n        for _stage, T_c, _from_sym, _to_sym, a, _b, _desc in _TRANSITIONS:\n            if T > T_c:\n                denominator = 2.0 * a * abs(T - T_c)\n                if denominator < 1e-10:\n                    return 1e10  # Divergence at T_c\n                return 1.0 / denominator\n        return 0.0\n\n    def free_energy_landscape(\n        self, T_range: tuple[float, float] = (0.001, 200.0), n_points: int = 200\n    ) -> dict[str, list[float]]:\n        \"\"\"Compute the Landau free energy across a temperature range.\n\n        Returns arrays for plotting F(T) with phase transition markers.\n        \"\"\"\n        temperatures = np.linspace(T_range[0], T_range[1], n_points).tolist()\n        free_energies = []\n        susceptibilities = []\n\n        for T in temperatures:\n            # F(T) = Σ [a(T-Tc)φ² + bφ⁴]\n            F = 0.0\n            for _stage, T_c, _from, _to, a, b, _desc in _TRANSITIONS:\n                phi = self._compute_order_parameter(T, T_c, a, b)\n                F += a * (T - T_c) * phi**2 + b * phi**4\n            free_energies.append(F)\n            susceptibilities.append(self.susceptibility(T))\n\n        critical_temperatures = [T_c for _, T_c, *_ in _TRANSITIONS]\n\n        return {\n            \"temperatures\": temperatures,\n            \"free_energies\": free_energies,\n            \"susceptibilities\": susceptibilities,\n            \"critical_temperatures\": critical_temperatures,\n        }\n\n\n# Singleton for the API\n_COSMOGONY: SymmetryBreaking | None = None\n\n\ndef get_cosmogony() -> SymmetryBreaking:\n    \"\"\"Get or create the singleton cosmogony instance.\"\"\"\n    global _COSMOGONY\n    if _COSMOGONY is None:\n        _COSMOGONY = SymmetryBreaking()\n    return _COSMOGONY\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"CosmogonyState\",\n    \"PhaseTransitionEvent\",\n    \"SymmetryBreaking\",\n    \"SymmetryGroup\",\n    \"ZeroAlgebra\",\n    \"get_cosmogony\",\n]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Riemannian geometry for the 12D axiomatic manifold.\n\nProvides the metric tensor, Christoffel symbols, geodesic equation,\nand curvature for the manifold on which agent trajectories evolve.\n\nThe metric tensor g_ij defines:\n  - Distances: ds² = g_ij dx^i dx^j\n  - Kinetic energy: T = ½ g_ij ẋ^i ẋ^j\n  - Geodesics (free particle paths): ẍ^i + Γ^i_jk ẋ^j ẋ^k = 0\n  - Curvature (how the manifold bends)\n\nIn the Genesis Engine, the metric is NOT Euclidean — it encodes the\nphysics of the four fabrics. The Fisher information metric (Milestone 4)\nwill provide the principled derivation; here we provide the computational\ninfrastructure.\n\nReferences:\n  - do Carmo (1992): Riemannian Geometry\n  - Nakahara (2003): Geometry, Topology and Physics, Ch. 7\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom typing import Callable\n\nimport numpy as np\nfrom scipy.integrate import solve_ivp\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass RiemannianMetric:\n    \"\"\"A Riemannian metric on an n-dimensional manifold.\n\n    The metric can be:\n    - Constant (same g_ij everywhere) — e.g., Euclidean, hyperbolic\n    - Position-dependent (callable) — e.g., Fisher metric, curved manifold\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    dim : int\n        Dimension of the manifold.\n    metric_fn : callable or np.ndarray\n        If callable: metric_fn(x) → (dim, dim) positive-definite matrix.\n        If ndarray: constant metric tensor (dim, dim).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        dim: int,\n        metric_fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray] | np.ndarray | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self.dim = dim\n\n        if metric_fn is None:\n            # Default: Euclidean (identity metric)\n            self._metric_fn = lambda _x: np.eye(dim)\n        elif isinstance(metric_fn, np.ndarray):\n            g = metric_fn.copy()\n            self._metric_fn = lambda _x: g\n        else:\n            self._metric_fn = metric_fn\n\n    def evaluate(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute metric tensor g_ij at point x.\"\"\"\n        return self._metric_fn(x)\n\n    def inverse(self, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute inverse metric g^ij at point x.\"\"\"\n        return np.linalg.inv(self.evaluate(x))\n\n    def determinant(self, x: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute det(g_ij) at point x.\"\"\"\n        return float(np.linalg.det(self.evaluate(x)))\n\n    def distance_squared(self, x: np.ndarray, dx: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute ds² = g_ij dx^i dx^j.\"\"\"\n        g = self.evaluate(x)\n        return float(dx @ g @ dx)\n\n    def norm(self, x: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute |v|_g = sqrt(g_ij v^i v^j) at point x.\"\"\"\n        return float(np.sqrt(max(self.distance_squared(x, v), 0.0)))\n\n    def christoffel(self, x: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-5) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute Christoffel symbols Γ^i_jk at point x.\n\n        Uses numerical differentiation of the metric tensor:\n        Γ^i_jk = ½ g^il (∂_j g_lk + ∂_k g_jl - ∂_l g_jk)\n\n        Returns shape (dim, dim, dim) array where result[i, j, k] = Γ^i_jk.\n        \"\"\"\n        n = self.dim\n        g_inv = self.inverse(x)\n\n        # Compute ∂_m g_ab numerically\n        dg = np.zeros((n, n, n))  # dg[m, a, b] = ∂_m g_ab\n        for m in range(n):\n            x_plus = x.copy()\n            x_minus = x.copy()\n            x_plus[m] += eps\n            x_minus[m] -= eps\n            dg[m] = (self.evaluate(x_plus) - self.evaluate(x_minus)) / (2 * eps)\n\n        # Γ^i_jk = ½ g^il (∂_j g_lk + ∂_k g_jl - ∂_l g_jk)\n        gamma = np.zeros((n, n, n))\n        for i in range(n):\n            for j in range(n):\n                for k in range(n):\n                    s = 0.0\n                    for l in range(n):\n                        s += g_inv[i, l] * (dg[j, l, k] + dg[k, j, l] - dg[l, j, k])\n                    gamma[i, j, k] = 0.5 * s\n\n        return gamma\n\n    def geodesic_acceleration(\n        self, x: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-5\n    ) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute geodesic acceleration: a^i = -Γ^i_jk v^j v^k.\n\n        This is the right-hand side of the geodesic equation:\n        ẍ^i = -Γ^i_jk ẋ^j ẋ^k\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        x : position on the manifold\n        v : velocity (tangent vector)\n        \"\"\"\n        gamma = self.christoffel(x, eps)\n        n = self.dim\n        accel = np.zeros(n)\n        for i in range(n):\n            for j in range(n):\n                for k in range(n):\n                    accel[i] -= gamma[i, j, k] * v[j] * v[k]\n        return accel\n\n    def geodesic(\n        self,\n        x0: np.ndarray,\n        v0: np.ndarray,\n        t_span: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),\n        n_steps: int = 100,\n    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n        \"\"\"Compute a geodesic starting from x0 with initial velocity v0.\n\n        Solves the geodesic equation ẍ^i + Γ^i_jk ẋ^j ẋ^k = 0.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        t : np.ndarray, shape (n_steps,)\n        trajectory : np.ndarray, shape (n_steps, dim)\n        \"\"\"\n        n = self.dim\n\n        def ode_rhs(t: float, state: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n            x = state[:n]\n            v = state[n:]\n            a = self.geodesic_acceleration(x, v)\n            return np.concatenate([v, a])\n\n        y0 = np.concatenate([x0, v0])\n        t_eval = np.linspace(t_span[0], t_span[1], n_steps)\n\n        sol = solve_ivp(ode_rhs, t_span, y0, t_eval=t_eval, method=\"RK45\", rtol=1e-8)\n\n        return sol.t, sol.y[:n].T  # (n_steps,) and (n_steps, dim)\n\n    def riemann_curvature_scalar(self, x: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-4) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute the Ricci scalar curvature R at point x.\n\n        R = g^ij R_ij where R_ij is the Ricci tensor (trace of Riemann tensor).\n\n        For the Euclidean metric, R = 0. For a sphere of radius r, R = 2/r².\n        This is an expensive computation (O(n⁵) for n dimensions).\n        \"\"\"\n        n = self.dim\n        g_inv = self.inverse(x)\n\n        # Compute Christoffel symbols and their derivatives\n        gamma = self.christoffel(x, eps)\n\n        # ∂_m Γ^i_jk\n        dgamma = np.zeros((n, n, n, n))\n        for m in range(n):\n            x_plus = x.copy()\n            x_minus = x.copy()\n            x_plus[m] += eps\n            x_minus[m] -= eps\n            dgamma[m] = (self.christoffel(x_plus, eps) - self.christoffel(x_minus, eps)) / (2 * eps)\n\n        # Riemann tensor R^i_jkl = ∂_k Γ^i_jl - ∂_l Γ^i_jk + Γ^i_km Γ^m_jl - Γ^i_lm Γ^m_jk\n        # Ricci tensor R_jl = R^i_jil\n        ricci = np.zeros((n, n))\n        for j in range(n):\n            for l in range(n):\n                for i in range(n):\n                    ricci[j, l] += dgamma[i, i, j, l] - dgamma[l, i, j, i]\n                    for m in range(n):\n                        ricci[j, l] += gamma[i, i, m] * gamma[m, j, l] - gamma[i, l, m] * gamma[m, j, i]\n\n        # Ricci scalar R = g^jl R_jl\n        R = 0.0\n        for j in range(n):\n            for l in range(n):\n                R += g_inv[j, l] * ricci[j, l]\n\n        return float(R)\n\n\n# --- Common metric constructors ---\n\n\ndef euclidean_metric(dim: int) -> RiemannianMetric:\n    \"\"\"Flat Euclidean metric: g_ij = δ_ij.\"\"\"\n    return RiemannianMetric(dim)\n\n\ndef hiho_metric(dim: int = 12, sigma: float = 0.3) -> RiemannianMetric:\n    \"\"\"HIHO-weighted metric: distances are larger near 0.5 (the attractor).\n\n    This makes the HIHO point a \"deep valley\" in the metric — geodesics\n    curve toward it naturally. The metric is:\n\n    g_ij(x) = δ_ij * (1 + λ * exp(-|x - 0.5|²/σ²))\n\n    where λ controls how deep the HIHO well is.\n    \"\"\"\n    target = np.full(dim, 0.5)\n\n    def metric_fn(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        dist_sq = np.sum((x - target) ** 2)\n        weight = 1.0 + 2.0 * np.exp(-dist_sq / sigma**2)\n        return np.eye(dim) * weight\n\n    return RiemannianMetric(dim, metric_fn)\n\n\ndef fabric_block_metric(dim: int = 12) -> RiemannianMetric:\n    \"\"\"Block-diagonal metric reflecting the four-fabric structure.\n\n    Each fabric (3 dims) has its own coupling constant:\n    - Space (dims 0-2): g₁ = 1.0\n    - Field (dims 3-5): g₂ = 0.7\n    - Control (dims 6-8): g₃ = 0.5\n    - Precipitation (dims 9-11): g₄ = 0.3\n\n    This encodes the gauge coupling constants from the plan.\n    \"\"\"\n    couplings = [1.0] * 3 + [0.7] * 3 + [0.5] * 3 + [0.3] * 3\n    g = np.diag(couplings)\n    return RiemannianMetric(dim, g)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"RiemannianMetric\",\n    \"euclidean_metric\",\n    \"fabric_block_metric\",\n    \"hiho_metric\",\n]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Lagrangian dynamics on the 12D axiomatic manifold.\n\nReplaces the ad-hoc `_toward_target()` linear interpolation in engine.py\nwith principled variational mechanics. Agent trajectories follow paths\nthat minimize the action integral S = ∫L dt.\n\nThe Lagrangian:\n    L(q, q̇) = T - V\n\nwhere:\n    T = ½ g_ij(q) q̇^i q̇^j       (Riemannian kinetic energy)\n    V = V_HIHO(q) + V_fabric(q)   (HIHO attractor + fabric potentials)\n\nThe Euler-Lagrange equations yield the geodesic equation with forces:\n    g_ij q̈^j + Γ^i_jk q̇^j q̇^k = -g^ij ∂V/∂q^j\n\nUses a symplectic (Störmer-Verlet) integrator for energy conservation.\n\nReferences:\n    - Arnold (1989): Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics\n    - Goldstein (2002): Classical Mechanics, Ch. 2\n    - Hairer, Lubich, Wanner (2006): Geometric Numerical Integration\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nfrom cohezion.physics.riemannian_metric import RiemannianMetric\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass Potential:\n    \"\"\"A potential energy function V(q) on the manifold.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    potential_fn : callable\n        Maps position q → scalar energy V(q).\n    gradient_fn : callable or None\n        Maps position q → gradient ∂V/∂q. If None, computed numerically.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        potential_fn: callable,\n        gradient_fn: callable | None = None,\n    ) -> None:\n        self._V = potential_fn\n        self._dV = gradient_fn\n\n    def evaluate(self, q: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute V(q).\"\"\"\n        return float(self._V(q))\n\n    def gradient(self, q: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-6) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute ∂V/∂q^i.\"\"\"\n        if self._dV is not None:\n            return self._dV(q)\n\n        # Numerical gradient\n        n = len(q)\n        grad = np.zeros(n)\n        for i in range(n):\n            q_plus = q.copy()\n            q_minus = q.copy()\n            q_plus[i] += eps\n            q_minus[i] -= eps\n            grad[i] = (self._V(q_plus) - self._V(q_minus)) / (2 * eps)\n        return grad\n\n\nclass LagrangianDynamics:\n    \"\"\"Euler-Lagrange dynamics on a Riemannian manifold with potential.\n\n    Parameters\n    ----------\n    metric : RiemannianMetric\n        The Riemannian metric g_ij defining kinetic energy.\n    potential : Potential\n        The potential energy V(q).\n    damping : float\n        Optional viscous damping coefficient (0 = conservative).\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        metric: RiemannianMetric,\n        potential: Potential,\n        damping: float = 0.0,\n    ) -> None:\n        self.metric = metric\n        self.potential = potential\n        self.damping = damping\n\n    def lagrangian(self, q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute L = T - V at (q, v).\"\"\"\n        T = 0.5 * self.metric.distance_squared(q, v)\n        V = self.potential.evaluate(q)\n        return T - V\n\n    def kinetic_energy(self, q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"T = ½ g_ij q̇^i q̇^j.\"\"\"\n        return 0.5 * self.metric.distance_squared(q, v)\n\n    def total_energy(self, q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        \"\"\"E = T + V (conserved for time-independent L without damping).\"\"\"\n        return self.kinetic_energy(q, v) + self.potential.evaluate(q)\n\n    def acceleration(self, q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Compute acceleration from Euler-Lagrange equations.\n\n        q̈^i = -Γ^i_jk q̇^j q̇^k - g^{ij} ∂V/∂q^j - γ q̇^i\n\n        where γ is the damping coefficient.\n        \"\"\"\n        # Geodesic term: -Γ^i_jk v^j v^k\n        geodesic = self.metric.geodesic_acceleration(q, v)\n\n        # Force term: -g^{ij} ∂V/∂q^j\n        g_inv = self.metric.inverse(q)\n        grad_V = self.potential.gradient(q)\n        force = -g_inv @ grad_V\n\n        # Damping term: -γ v^i\n        damp = -self.damping * v\n\n        return geodesic + force + damp\n\n    def step_verlet(\n        self, q: np.ndarray, v: np.ndarray, dt: float\n    ) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:\n        \"\"\"One step of Störmer-Verlet (leapfrog) integration.\n\n        Symplectic: preserves the geometric structure of Hamilton's equations.\n        Energy drift is bounded (no secular growth) unlike RK4.\n        \"\"\"\n        a = self.acceleration(q, v)\n        v_half = v + 0.5 * dt * a\n        q_new = q + dt * v_half\n        a_new = self.acceleration(q_new, v_half)\n        v_new = v_half + 0.5 * dt * a_new\n        return q_new, v_new\n\n    def simulate(\n        self,\n        q0: np.ndarray,\n        v0: np.ndarray,\n        n_steps: int = 100,\n        dt: float = 0.01,\n    ) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:\n        \"\"\"Simulate a trajectory from initial conditions.\n\n        Returns dict with:\n        - positions: (n_steps+1, dim)\n        - velocities: (n_steps+1, dim)\n        - energies: (n_steps+1,) — total energy at each step\n        - lagrangians: (n_steps+1,) — L at each step\n        \"\"\"\n        dim = len(q0)\n        positions = np.zeros((n_steps + 1, dim))\n        velocities = np.zeros((n_steps + 1, dim))\n        energies = np.zeros(n_steps + 1)\n        lagrangians = np.zeros(n_steps + 1)\n\n        q, v = q0.copy(), v0.copy()\n        positions[0] = q\n        velocities[0] = v\n        energies[0] = self.total_energy(q, v)\n        lagrangians[0] = self.lagrangian(q, v)\n\n        for i in range(1, n_steps + 1):\n            q, v = self.step_verlet(q, v, dt)\n            positions[i] = q\n            velocities[i] = v\n            energies[i] = self.total_energy(q, v)\n            lagrangians[i] = self.lagrangian(q, v)\n\n        return {\n            \"positions\": positions,\n            \"velocities\": velocities,\n            \"energies\": energies,\n            \"lagrangians\": lagrangians,\n        }\n\n    def action_integral(\n        self, trajectory: np.ndarray, dt: float\n    ) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute the action S = ∫L dt along a discrete trajectory.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        trajectory : (n_steps, dim)\n        dt : time step between trajectory points\n        \"\"\"\n        S = 0.0\n        for i in range(len(trajectory) - 1):\n            q = trajectory[i]\n            v = (trajectory[i + 1] - trajectory[i]) / dt\n            S += self.lagrangian(q, v) * dt\n        return S\n\n\n# --- Common potential constructors ---\n\n\ndef hiho_potential(dim: int = 12, sigma: float = 0.3, depth: float = 1.0) -> Potential:\n    \"\"\"HIHO attractor potential: Gaussian well at coherence = 0.5.\n\n    V(q) = -depth * exp(-|q - 0.5|² / σ²) + soft_wall\n\n    The agent is naturally drawn to the HIHO point (all dimensions at 0.5).\n    \"\"\"\n    target = np.full(dim, 0.5)\n\n    def V(q: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        dist_sq = np.sum((q - target) ** 2)\n        return -depth * np.exp(-dist_sq / sigma**2) + 0.05 * dist_sq\n\n    def dV(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        diff = q - target\n        dist_sq = np.sum(diff**2)\n        gauss = np.exp(-dist_sq / sigma**2)\n        return 2 * depth * diff * gauss / sigma**2 + 0.1 * diff\n\n    return Potential(V, dV)\n\n\ndef harmonic_potential(dim: int = 12, k: float = 1.0, center: np.ndarray | None = None) -> Potential:\n    \"\"\"Simple harmonic potential V = k/2 |q - center|².\"\"\"\n    if center is None:\n        center = np.full(dim, 0.5)\n\n    def V(q: np.ndarray) -> float:\n        return 0.5 * k * float(np.sum((q - center) ** 2))\n\n    def dV(q: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        return k * (q - center)\n\n    return Potential(V, dV)\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"LagrangianDynamics\",\n    \"Potential\",\n    \"harmonic_potential\",\n    \"hiho_potential\",\n]\n"
}

  "content": "\"\"\"Tests for Riemannian geometry and Lagrangian dynamics.\n\nVerifies mathematical properties: flat metric → straight geodesics,\nenergy conservation, action stationarity, Christoffel symbol identities.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport numpy as np\nimport pytest\n\nfrom cohezion.physics.lagrangian import (\n    LagrangianDynamics,\n    Potential,\n    harmonic_potential,\n    hiho_potential,\n)\nfrom cohezion.physics.riemannian_metric import (\n    RiemannianMetric,\n    euclidean_metric,\n    fabric_block_metric,\n    hiho_metric,\n)\n\n\nclass TestEuclideanMetric:\n    \"\"\"Verify properties of flat (Euclidean) metric.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_euclidean_is_identity(self):\n        \"\"\"g_ij = δ_ij for Euclidean metric.\"\"\"\n        m = euclidean_metric(3)\n        x = np.array([1.0, 2.0, 3.0])\n        np.testing.assert_array_equal(m.evaluate(x), np.eye(3))\n\n    def test_euclidean_inverse_is_identity(self):\n        \"\"\"g^ij = δ^ij for Euclidean   "content": "\"\"\"Fiber bundle structure for the 12D axiomatic manifold.\n\nThe 12D manifold M¹² has a natural principal fiber bundle structure:\n\n  P(B⁴, G) where G = SO(3)⁴\n\n  Total space: M¹² = Space(3) × Field(3) × Control(3) × Precipitation(3)\n  Base space:  B⁴  = (‖Space‖, ‖Field‖, ‖Control‖, ‖Precip‖)\n  Fiber:       F⁸  = internal directions within each fabric\n\nThe base projection π maps each 12D point to its 4D \"macroscopic\" state\n(how much of each fabric), while the fiber encodes the internal configuration\n(which direction within each fabric).\n\nThe connection 1-form ω defines parallel transport — how internal states\nevolve as agents move through the base space. The curvature Ω = dω + ω∧ω\nmeasures field strength (deviation from HIHO flat connection).\n\nReferences:\n  - Nakahara (2003): Geometry, Topology and Physics, Ch. 9-10\n  - Kobayashi & Nomizu (1963): Foundations of Differential Geometry\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n\nimport numpy as np\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n# Fabric indices: which 3 of the 12 dimensions belong to each fabric\nFABRIC_SLICES = {\n    \"Space\": slice(0, 3),\n    \"Field\": slice(3, 6),\n    \"Control\": slice(6, 9),\n    \"Precipitation\": slice(9, 12),\n}\n\nFABRIC_NAMES = list(FABRIC_SLICES.keys())\n\n\n@dataclass\nclass FiberBundleState:\n    \"\"\"Decomposed state showing base-space and fiber components.\n\n    Attributes\n    ----------\n    base : np.ndarray, shape (4,)\n        Base-space coordinates (fabric norms): [‖Space‖, ‖Field‖, ‖Control‖, ‖Precip‖]\n    fiber : np.ndarray, shape (4, 3)\n        Fiber state: unit direction vectors within each fabric.\n        fiber[i] = normalized direction in fabric i.\n    raw : np.ndarray, shape (12,)\n        Original 12D state.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    base: np.ndarray\n    fiber: np.ndarray\n    raw: np.ndarray\n\n    def to_dict(self) -> dict:\n        \"\"\"Serialize for API/SurrealDB.\"\"\"\n        return {\n            \"base\": self.base.tolist(),\n            \"fiber\": self.fiber.tolist(),\n            \"fabric_norms\": {\n                name: float(self.base[i]) for i, name in enumerate(FABRIC_NAMES)\n            },\n            \"fabric_directions\": {\n                name: self.fiber[i].tolist() for i, name in enumerate(FABRIC_NAMES)\n            },\n        }\n\n\nclass FiberBundle:\n    \"\"\"Principal fiber bundle P(B⁴, SO(3)⁴) over the fabric base space.\n\n    Provides decomposition, projection, parallel transport, and\n    curvature computation for the 12D axiomatic manifold.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dim: int = 12, n_fabrics: int = 4) -> None:\n        if dim != n_fabrics * 3:\n            raise ValueError(f\"dim must be n_fabrics * 3, got {dim} and {n_fabrics}\")\n        self.dim = dim\n        self.n_fabrics = n_fabrics\n        self.fabric_dim = 3\n\n    def decompose(self, state_12d: np.ndarray) -> FiberBundleState:\n        \"\"\"Decompose a 12D state into base-space + fiber components.\n\n        Base: π(q) = (‖q_Space‖, ‖q_Field‖, ‖q_Control‖, ‖q_Precip‖)\n        Fiber: normalized direction within each fabric triplet.\n        \"\"\"\n        state = np.asarray(state_12d, dtype=np.float64)\n        base = np.zeros(self.n_fabrics)\n        fiber = np.zeros((self.n_fabrics, self.fabric_dim))\n\n        for i, (name, sl) in enumerate(FABRIC_SLICES.items()):\n            block = state[sl]\n            norm = np.linalg.norm(block)\n            base[i] = norm\n            fiber[i] = block / norm if norm > 1e-15 else np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])\n\n        return FiberBundleState(base=base, fiber=fiber, raw=state.copy())\n\n    def project_to_base(self, state_12d: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Canonical projection π: M¹² → B⁴.\n\n        Returns the four fabric norms.\n        \"\"\"\n        return self.decompose(state_12d).base\n\n    def reconstruct(self, base: np.ndarray, fiber: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Reconstruct 12D state from base + fiber.\n\n        state[fabric_i] = base[i] * fiber[i]\n        \"\"\"\n        state = np.zeros(self.dim)\n        for i, (_name, sl) in enumerate(FABRIC_SLICES.items()):\n            direction = fiber[i] / np.linalg.norm(fiber[i]) if np.linalg.norm(fiber[i]) > 1e-15 else np.array([1.0, 0.0, 0.0])\n            state[sl] = base[i] * direction\n        return state\n\n    def horizontal_component(\n        self, state_12d: np.ndarray, tangent_12d: np.ndarray\n    ) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Extract horizontal (base-space) component of a tangent vector.\n\n        The horizontal component changes the fabric norms (base coordinates)\n        without changing the internal directions (fiber coordinates).\n\n        For a flat connection, the horizontal component of v at q is:\n        v_H = sum_i (v_i · n_i) * n_i   (projection onto fabric directions)\n        \"\"\"\n        decomp = self.decompose(state_12d)\n        h = np.zeros(self.dim)\n\n        for i, (_name, sl) in enumerate(FABRIC_SLICES.items()):\n            v_block = tangent_12d[sl]\n            n = decomp.fiber[i]  # Unit direction in this fabric\n            # Horizontal part: component along the current fabric direction\n            h[sl] = np.dot(v_block, n) * n\n\n        return h\n\n    def vertical_component(\n        self, state_12d: np.ndarray, tangent_12d: np.ndarray\n    ) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Extract vertical (fiber) component of a tangent vector.\n\n        The vertical component changes internal directions without\n        changing fabric norms. v_V = v - v_H.\n        \"\"\"\n        return tangent_12d - self.horizontal_component(state_12d, tangent_12d)\n\n    def connection_form(\n        self, state_12d: np.ndarray, tangent_12d: np.ndarray\n    ) -> np.ndarray:\n        \"\"\"Evaluate the connection 1-form ω(v) at a point.\n\n        For a flat connection: ω(v) = v_V (the vertical component).\n        Returns a (4, 3) array — one so(3) element per fabric.\n\n        For a non-flat connection (gauge field active), this would include\n        the gauge potential A_μ. Currently implements the flat case.\n        \"\"\"\n        v_vert = self.vertical_component(state_12d, tangent_12d)\n        # Reshape into per-fabric Lie algebra elements\n        return v_vert.reshape(self.n_fabrics, self.fabric_dim)\n\n    def curvature_norm(\n        self,\n        state_12d: np.ndarray,\n        v1: np.ndarray,\n        v2: np.ndarray,\n    ) -> float:\n        \"\"\"Compute the norm of the curvature 2-form Ω(v1, v2).\n\n        For a flat connection, Ω = 0. Non-zero curvature indicates\n        that parallel transport is path-dependent — the gauge field\n        is active. This is the \"force\" that deflects agent trajectories.\n\n        Approximated as ‖[ω(v1), ω(v2)]‖ (Lie bracket of connection values).\n        \"\"\"\n        omega1 = self.connection_form(state_12d, v1)\n        omega2 = self.connection_form(state_12d, v2)\n\n        # Lie bracket [ω1, ω2] per fabric (cross product for so(3))\n        total_curvature = 0.0\n        for i in range(self.n_fabrics):\n            bracket = np.cross(omega1[i], omega2[i])\n            total_curvature += np.linalg.norm(bracket)\n\n        return total_curvature\n\n    def parallel_transport(\n        self,\n        fiber_state: np.ndarray,\n        base_curve: np.ndarray,\n    ) -> list[np.ndarray]:\n        \"\"\"Parallel transport fiber state along a base-space curve.\n\n        For a flat connection, parallel transport preserves the fiber\n        direction — the transported state is identical everywhere.\n\n        Parameters\n        ----------\n        fiber_state : (4, 3)\n            Initial fiber configuration (unit directions per fabric).\n        base_curve : (n_steps, 4)\n            Curve in base space to transport along.\n\n        Returns\n        -------\n        list of (4, 3) fiber states at each point of the curve.\n        \"\"\"\n        # For flat connection: fiber is constant along the curve\n        return [fiber_state.copy() for _ in range(len(base_curve))]\n\n    def fabric_curvature_per_fabric(\n        self,\n        trajectory_12d: np.ndarray,\n    ) -> dict[str, float]:\n        \"\"\"Compute per-fabric curvature from a 12D trajectory.\n\n        Measures how much the fiber direction changes along the trajectory\n        for each fabric. High curvature = the agent's internal state\n        is rotating rapidly within that fabric.\n        \"\"\"\n        n = len(trajectory_12d)\n        if n < 2:\n            return {name: 0.0 for name in FABRIC_NAMES}\n\n        curvatures = {}\n        for i, name in enumerate(FABRIC_NAMES):\n            sl = list(FABRIC_SLICES.values())[i]\n            total_angle = 0.0\n            for t in range(n - 1):\n                d1 = trajectory_12d[t, sl]\n                d2 = trajectory_12d[t + 1, sl]\n                n1 = np.linalg.norm(d1)\n                n2 = np.linalg.norm(d2)\n                if n1 > 1e-15 and n2 > 1e-15:\n                    cos_angle = np.clip(np.dot(d1, d2) / (n1 * n2), -1, 1)\n                    total_angle += np.arccos(cos_angle)\n\n            curvatures[name] = float(total_angle / max(n - 1, 1))\n\n        return curvatures\n\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"FABRIC_NAMES\",\n    \"FABRIC_SLICES\",\n    \"FiberBundle\",\n    \"FiberBundleState\",\n]\n"
}
